purpose: Ibandronate is used to treat and prevent osteoporosis in women after menopause. It helps reduce the risk of fractures, especially in the spine, by keeping your bones strong. Your doctor may prescribe it if a bone density test shows your bones are thinning.
how_it_works: Your body is constantly breaking down old bone and building new bone. In osteoporosis, too much bone is being broken down and not enough is being replaced. Ibandronate works by slowing down the cells that break your bone down, which helps keep your bones denser and stronger over time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include heartburn, upset stomach, nausea, belly pain, diarrhea, back pain, or muscle and joint aches. If you take the pill form, you may notice irritation in your esophagus (the tube connecting your mouth to your stomach) if it is not taken correctly.
warnings: Always take the tablet on an empty stomach first thing in the morning with a full glass of plain water (not juice or coffee). Stay upright — sitting or standing — for at least 60 minutes after taking it and do not eat or drink anything else during that time. This helps prevent serious irritation or damage to your esophagus. Rare but serious risks include jaw bone problems (osteonecrosis of the jaw) and unusual thigh bone fractures. Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, low calcium levels, or dental issues before starting this medication.
typical_dosing: The most common dose is one 150 mg tablet taken by mouth once a month, always on the same date each month. There is also an injectable form given by a healthcare provider every 3 months. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
